sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: The Prompt Engineering Guide from DAIR.AI is a free collection of guides, papers, lectures and tools on writing prompts for language models. It is published as the website promptingguide.ai and covers basics, techniques, applications, model notes and risks.
sixtySeconds.problem: Prompting techniques are spread across research papers and blog posts. This guide explains them in one place, from zero-shot and few-shot prompting to chain-of-thought, ReAct and retrieval-augmented generation, with examples.
whoFor: Students and researchers learning prompting techniques
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it as a free, well-known reference for prompting techniques and papers. It is reading material, not a tool; DAIR.AI also sells separate paid courses.
requirements: A web browser to read it online
Node.js 18+ and pnpm to run it locally

overview: The guide is organised into an introduction (LLM settings, prompt basics, prompt elements, tips and examples), techniques, applications, a prompt hub, model notes, risks and misuses, papers, tools, notebooks, datasets and further reading.

Techniques covered include zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, self-consistency, generated knowledge, prompt chaining, tree of thoughts, retrieval-augmented generation, automatic reasoning and tool use, automatic prompt engineer, ReAct, multimodal chain-of-thought and graph prompting. Applications include function calling, generating data and generating code.

The README links a one-hour lecture with a notebook and slides. The website version at promptingguide.ai is the most up to date, and the site can also be run locally with Nextra, for example to check a translation.
